about.title: Marysville Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Marysville is a small city of just over 12,000 people, and when a life is lost here the absence is felt on every block along 10th Street, E Street, 5th Street and B Street. The most recent final crash year, 2025, recorded 43 injury collisions, 66 people hurt and 3 traffic deaths within Marysville, here in Yuba County. Each of those numbers is a household changed forever. A wrongful death claim in California is a civil action, kept separate from any criminal charges the district attorney may or may not bring. The family, not the state, decides whether to pursue it. Standing is limited: a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The claim can seek funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive does not handle cases ourselves. We are a free service that connects Marysville families with an independent attorney who does, on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Marysville Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out who in your family holds the right to bring the claim before anything is filed.

items.title: The two-year clock is real
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Connecting early keeps those deadlines from quietly passing.

items.title: Independent of any criminal case
items.desc: A wrongful death claim is a civil matter and does not wait for, or depend on, a prosecutor's decision. The attorney you are matched with works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash near 10th Street in Marysville. Does a police report decide whether we have a claim?
items.answer: No. The collision report is one piece of evidence, but a civil wrongful death claim is decided separately from any traffic citation or criminal case. An independent attorney can review the report alongside witness accounts, vehicle data and other records to evaluate what happened. Getting that review started soon helps preserve evidence along busy corridors like 10th Street or E Street.

items.question: What losses can a wrongful death claim in California cover?
items.answer: California allows eligible family members to seek funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have contributed over their lifetime, and the loss of love, companionship, comfort and guidance. The specific amount depends entirely on the circumstances of the person and the family. No one can promise a particular result, and an attorney should be candid with you about that.

items.question: How long do we have to act, and what if a government vehicle was involved?
items.answer: The general deadline in California is two years from the date of death. If a public entity such as a city, county or state agency is potentially responsible, a separate administrative claim must be filed much sooner, often within six months. Because those shorter windows are easy to miss during a period of grief, speaking with an attorney early is worthwhile.
